name: Turbo Dash
description: A colorful endless runner platformer across ten named difficulty levels. Jump tripwires, ride springs, read portals, dodge crumbling and fake platforms, evolve mid-run, pop coin balloons, keep a pet, and chase a live shared leaderboard.
author: CaisoGames AI Team

keyboard.space: Jump (hold for a higher jump); start; resume; restart
keyboard.escape: Pause / resume; back out of any menu
keyboard.s: Shop (from the title, pause, LIFE LOST and game-over screens); JET dive during a run
keyboard.n: Set or change your leaderboard name (on the leaderboard)
keyboard.e: End the run (on the pause screen)
keyboard.arrows / WASD: Steer JET: hold to climb, DOWN/S dive, RIGHT/D boost, LEFT/A brake

mouse.click: Jump (hold for a higher jump); buttons; drag to steer JET
mouse.hover: Buttons lift and the cursor becomes a pointer; every button shows its key as a chip

touch.description: Tap anywhere to jump, hold for a higher jump, drag to steer JET. Pause button in the top-right. Both orientations, full screen.

viewport.world: 600 logical px tall, always. Ground at 450, ceiling at 18 - every measured physics figure in this file depends on those and none of them change.
viewport.landscape: Logical height 600; width follows the screen's aspect, clamped 800..1400. A wider phone sees further down the track.
viewport.portrait: Logical width 600; height follows the aspect (up to 1500). The ground is anchored at 70% of the screen with sky above and earth below. 600 wide, not 800, so the character is the same size in both orientations on the same phone; the cost is 450px of look-ahead instead of 650 (0.75s at top speed, 1.5s at the start).
viewport.hud: Drawn in screen space and pinned to the real edges.
viewport.menus: Laid out once for 800x600 and drawn through a uniform scale-to-fit transform (withUiSpace): 1.0 in landscape, 0.75 in portrait. Buttons remember the transform so taps map back through it.
viewport.hidpi: Backing store at device resolution (capped 2x); the game was blurry on every phone before.
viewport.measured: iPhone 17 Pro: 402x680 CSS px used of 402x681 in portrait, 756x351 of 756x352 in landscape - no letterbox either way; character 27px / 23px. Before: a 390x292 box in the middle of the landscape screen, and a 'rotate your device' nag in portrait.
viewport.turret: The pop range is clamped to the visible track (min(500, W - 180)), and the shell slowed 5.5 -> 4.5 so the pop-to-impact window stays above 30 frames on every screen at top speed.

features: Three-stage in-run evolution: RUNNER -> WINGED (double jump) -> BLAZE (triple jump + glide)
Evolution Cores earned by completing missions, collected on the track ahead
Air jumps set velocity rather than adding it, so every one is a reliable recovery
Each successive air jump is weaker, keeping the height ceiling bounded
Gap sizes scale with each form's MEASURED reach, so evolving never trivialises the level
Stage score multipliers (x1.0 / x1.25 / x1.6) reward evolving early
Form resets on death - losing a BLAZE run is the strongest restart pressure in the game
Coyote time and jump buffering so deaths always feel earned
Coin combo multiplier up to x8, plus close-call and big-air bonuses
Three rotating missions per run with per-mission difficulty tiers
Persistent records, rank and lifetime coins via localStorage
Power-ups: magnet, shield, and a temporary extra air jump
Four crossfading biomes: Meadow, Sunset Ridge, Midnight, Frost Peaks
Screen shake, hit-stop, speed lines and WebAudio sound with no asset files
Full touch support with multi-finger hold tracking and iOS audio unlock
Boot screen that explains itself if a sandboxed viewer blocks its scripts
Shop with three slots: hats, back packs and trails, bought with coins earned by playing
Strong items are gated on a distance RECORD as well as price - price alone gates time, not skill
Item effects chosen so none can inflate a score: the coin bonus pays the wallet only, and the slow pack trades scoring rate for reaction time
Cloud leaderboard over the artifact db capability: live top 20, one row per player
Name prompt via a real HTML input, so phones get their keyboard and accessibility
The game is complete without the cloud - the board falls back to this device's best
Three lives (max five), so one fall no longer ends the run
Reviving COSTS an evolution stage and the coin combo, which is what keeps scores comparable
Rare heart pickups that appear more often the closer you are to losing
Final-life tension: a pulsing red vignette kept to the screen edges so hazards stay readable
Super Suit: hold to fly from the opening second on a 12s tank that refills on the ground - permanent for the run, and no flight ever ends in a plunge
Ten named difficulty levels, each announcing the hazard it introduces
Crumbling platforms (level 3+) that shake, crack and collapse 0.8s after you land
Fake platforms (level 5+) placed as DECOYS in wide gaps, never on the route itself
Fakes carry a visible tell (translucent and drifting) so reading them is a skill, not a memory test
Coin balloons: a high, off-line jump that pays 60 coins straight into the wallet
Pets: Coin Pup (wallet-only coin gathering), Scout Bird (marks fakes), Spark Cub (spares one revive penalty)
A single banner queue, so zone, level and evolution announcements never overwrite each other
Fourth evolution HERO: 4 jumps plus a rechargeable flight burst, earned by completing all three missions in one run
HERO's flight refills only while running on the ground, so hovering forever is impossible by construction
The wallet total and a savings goal are shown during play, on the game-over screen and in the shop
Coins are banked the moment they are collected, so abandoning a run mid-way (app switch, closed tab) loses nothing
A storage self-test at boot; if saving is blocked the title screen says so instead of failing silently
Losing a life freezes the run on a LIFE LOST screen until a tap, with CONTINUE and SHOP offered there
Turrets (level 8+): a hatch that rises into a cannon, fires ONE knee-high shot back down the track, and sinks; only the shell hurts, and any jump clears it

The secret cloud: a near-transparent cloud along the top of the world, moving at WORLD speed rather than cloud speed, collected only on the third jump of one flight; pays coins, an instant HERO form, a free (record-eligible) shop item, or every life back
Fifth evolution JET: drag to fly - climb, dive, boost or brake - on a five-second tank that refills only on the ground, with jet flames and a gauge beside the character

Sixth evolution SPIDER: hold to jump then web-swing, release to drop with the swing's speed, press again to web again; three webs per flight, refilled by landing, and the web lets go by itself before it could swing you backward
Finished missions are re-rolled during the run, so there are always three live goals and the five cores to SPIDER are reachable
Every change is written to storage at once - no throttle, no unsaved window
Two on-disk copies: the previous state is rotated to a backup before each write, and a corrupt primary is recovered from it and repaired on the spot
Writes fire on pagehide, beforeunload, blur, freeze and visibilitychange, plus a 1s heartbeat while playing
A tick lights beside the wallet on every successful save, so saving is something the player can watch happen
Tripwires (level 2+): the first hazard, and the only one that never kills - run into one and you stumble for 0.37s with no jump
A wire is only placed where the platform runs on for the whole stun distance at top speed, so a stumble can never end at a pit
Springs (level 4+): a high, slow arc under halved gravity - long enough to see the landing and steer with an air jump
Portals (level 7+): both rings drawn so the exit is readable first; a warp pays +150 but skips the loot between and spends your air jumps
Skipped portal distance is never credited to distance, level, biome or speed
A 0.45s input lockout when the run stops, so the taps already in flight at the moment of death cannot dismiss the screen
LIFE LOST accepts only its CONTINUE button - never a stray tap - and shows WAIT while locked
A pause button in the top-right corner, with a PAUSED screen offering RESUME, SHOP, LEADERBOARD and END RUN
Escape toggles pause; a menu opened from the pause returns to the pause rather than into a running game

primary: Multi-jump physics with coyote time and jump buffering
unique: Missions pay out a visible ability rather than an abstract score bonus
A power curve inside a single run: weak, strong, unstoppable
Form is lost on death, so loss aversion drives the restart
Gaps sized from each form's measured physics, not an estimate
Shop perks are designed so buying power cannot buy leaderboard position
A revive costs a form and the combo, so three lives inflate scores x1.78 rather than the naive x3
Flight is a total budget per run, making WHEN to spend it the decision rather than whether to hold
Fake platforms are opt-in bait beside the route, so a trap is never a coin flip
Mid-run shopping is a pickup rather than a menu, because a menu would stop the run
Pets may ease the run or fatten the wallet, but never inflate the score
Flight is reachable by skill (HERO) as well as by purchase, keeping the game's rule that strong powers are earned
HERO's short rechargeable burst and the Super Suit's large one-shot budget stay distinct, so buying the suit still buys something
The stumble is the only non-lethal hazard, so it is the first one taught
A spring's slowness is its fairness: the arc is long enough to react to
A portal shows its exit before you commit, and costs air jumps and loot, so it is a decision rather than a gift
The stop screens are guarded against in-flight input, because a runner is played by tapping constantly
LIFE LOST is a decision screen so it needs a deliberate button; game over is a restart screen so tap-to-restart survives the lockout

difficulty.principle: One new hazard per level, never two, so there is always a stretch to learn each.

knownLimitations: Must be opened in a real browser or from a web address. In-app file previews (the sheet with an x and a share button) sandbox the page and block its scripts via CSP, which fires no error and does not trigger <noscript>; the game detects this and shows an explanation instead of a blank canvas.
Leaderboard identity is a per-browser id with a self-declared name. There is no verified user identity available to the page, so it is a friendly board rather than an anti-cheat system.

stages.name: WINGED
stages.earnedBy: Complete one mission during the run, then collect the Evolution Core

stages.name: BLAZE
stages.earnedBy: Complete a second mission, then collect the next Core

stages.name: HERO
stages.earnedBy: Complete a third mission in the same run, then collect the Core

stages.name: JET
stages.grants: Drag to fly: climb, dive, boost (+45% scroll) or brake (-30%). 5s tank, refills only on the ground. Jumps return when the tank is dry.
stages.earnedBy: A fourth mission in the same run (missions re-roll), then the Core
stages.control: Touch: drag from wherever the finger went down; a held tap without movement climbs. Keyboard: hold to climb, DOWN/S dive, RIGHT/D boost, LEFT/A brake.
stages.gaps: Sized for HERO's jumps, never for flight - an empty tank is never a death sentence.

stages.name: SPIDER
stages.grants: Hold to jump, keep holding and a web fires at the apex to a point 150px ahead and 170px up; swing under it. Release to drop with the swing's momentum. Press again in the air for another web. Three webs per flight, refilled by landing. No air jumps.
stages.earnedBy: A fifth mission in the same run, then the Core
stages.physics: A real pendulum in world space, position-based; its horizontal velocity IS the scroll for that frame, so the world rushes past at the bottom of the swing. The web lets go by itself the instant the swing would carry you backward.
stages.measured: One swing = 3.25x RUNNER's reach at the same speed; two chained = 4.92x; three = 6.56x. Gaps use 2.95 (HERO's), so a single swing clears the hardest gap with ~10% to spare.
stages.whyABudget: Without the three-web cap a held button chained swings along the ceiling forever. Every flying form here keeps the rule that hovering forever is impossible by construction.

progression.note: Evolution is per-run and resets on death. Missions are re-rolled as they finish, so the climb to SPIDER takes five missions in one run. Mission tiers persist, so cores get harder to earn over time.
progression.naming: The two new forms are deliberately named JET and SPIDER rather than after any trademarked character: the game is published publicly. The mechanics - drag flight with a fuel bar, web swinging - are the part that was asked for and they are all here.

shop.currency: Coins collected while running, banked into a wallet at the end of each run
shop.designRule: Nothing sold may inflate a score. Coin bonuses pay the wallet only; the slow pack reduces scoring rate as well as difficulty; the strongest two items additionally require a distance record, because a price tag gates patience rather than skill.

items.effect: start each run with a shield
world 8% slower - and scoring 8% slower with it
Gathers coins; they pay the wallet, never the score
Once a run, a revive costs no evolution stage
Hold to fly from the opening second; 12s per run, then a Turbo Pack

leaderboard.shape: One document per player keyed by a per-browser id; live top 20 via orderBy(score,desc).limit(20).onSnapshot
leaderboard.identity: Self-declared name in localStorage. No verified user identity is available to the page, so this is a friendly board, not anti-cheat.
leaderboard.degradation: Outside the artifact viewer there is no window.claude at all, so the board falls back to this device's own best and the game is otherwise unchanged.
leaderboard.constraint: The db capability cannot be combined with public sharing, so the cloud build is organization-internal. A separate public build ships without db.
leaderboard.untrustedInput: Rows are written by other viewers: names are stripped of control characters and capped, and numbers are coerced before display.

lives.reviveCost: One evolution stage and the entire coin combo
lives.measuredInflation: x1.78 average score vs a single life, against a naive expectation of x3
lives.hearts: Rare pickups. Spawn chance is 0 at full health and rises to ~9% per platform on the last life.

coinBalloon.form: A balloon on the track, floating off the safe line, reached with a deliberate jump
coinBalloon.wasPreviously: A MERCHANT balloon that SOLD a power-up for 60 coins out of the wallet.
coinBalloon.whyItChanged: The wallet had two jobs at once - long-term savings for the shop, and the merchant's in-run currency - and they fought. A player who met two balloons in one run earned 78 coins and finished with 42 FEWER than they started with, while the end screen reported '+78 this run'. Nothing was lost and nothing was broken; the game spent the savings and never said so, which reads exactly like a bug. For children, who play to watch a number go up, a mechanic that eats the number is worse than no mechanic.
coinBalloon.whatWasKept: The decision. It still floats high and off the line, so reaching it is a real jump with a landing to think about - but the stake is risk, which is free, instead of savings, which accumulate slowly.
coinBalloon.whatWasDropped: Selling powers. Shields, magnets and wings already fall free from the world and hearts have their own pickup that scales with trouble, so the merchant was a second, worse door to things that already had one. powerChance rose from 0.05/0.11 to 0.07/0.14 to carry its share.
coinBalloon.balanceRule: Balloon coins pay the WALLET and never the SCORE, exactly like the Crown and the Pup. The Crown's +25% applies. Counted apart from stats.runCoins so a lucky balloon cannot finish a 'collect ten coins' mission.
coinBalloon.whyFasterCoinsAreSafe: Leaderboard position is protected by needBest - a distance RECORD - not by price. Price gates patience; records gate skill. Making coins flow faster speeds up the shop without weakening the thing the economy exists to protect.
coinBalloon.measuredIncome: Per run, assuming every coin is caught: 1000m ~118, 3000m ~286, 6000m ~648. At the ~40% catch rate a real 6000m run showed, that is roughly 4x the old income - and the old figure was before the merchant took 60 per balloon back out.

turret.range: Pops when the player is within 500px; hatch light blinks red from 800px
turret.timing: 18 frames to rise (the cue), one shot, 8 frames up, 18 to sink. From the pop to impact at top speed: 32 frames (~0.53s at 10px/frame, ~0.6s at typical speeds).
turret.shot: Knee height, 5.5px/frame on top of the scroll. Any jump clears it; a shield absorbs it; hitting it costs a life like a spike.
turret.placement: Ground platforms only, past the landing zone, 110px clear of spikes, wires and springs. Never on floating slabs.
turret.whyOnlyTheShellHurts: A solid block rising out of the floor under a committed jump would be an unreadable death. The cannon body is scenery; it has usually sunk again by the time you reach it.
turret.alsoFixed: A revive slid platforms, coins, spikes, pickups and cores forward but left wires, springs and portals behind, so a revive could put a tripwire in mid-air. Every layer moves together now.

secretCloud.where: y=44, the summit of the world. Spawns 2.2% per platform once the player has a third jump (BLAZE+), one at a time.
secretCloud.tell: It scrolls at world speed (1.0x) while real clouds drift at 0.2x. Alpha 0.18-0.34 in the biome's cloud colour, no glow, no outline, no bob. Nobody is told; it can only be noticed.
secretCloud.whyTheThirdJump: A held double jump already reaches the ceiling (measured: player top 26px vs ceiling 18px), so height gates nothing. Counting jumps in one flight - ground + 2 air = 3 - makes it a move you have to know, and a flying form cannot stumble into it.
secretCloud.prizes: coins 300 (w40), instant HERO (w22), a free shop item the player's RECORD already qualifies them for (w22), 1000 coins (w8), all lives (w8). Coins are wallet-only. HERO is per-run. Fallbacks to coins when a prize would be useless.
secretCloud.whyNot6000Coins: 6000 is ~40% of the whole shop in one touch, and a good BLAZE run meets several clouds. 300/1000 keep it a jackpot without collapsing the economy; the free item and the instant HERO are the prizes that feel big.

portalExits.measuredBefore: 35-41% of generator-placed portals ever resolved an exit, per level. The rest were drawn and inert - a ring you ran into that did nothing.
portalExits.fix: Two parts. resolvePortalExits accepts any real platform that OVERLAPS the warp window with 80px of landing room, not only one that starts inside it (that alone reached ~70%). And generatePlatform, when it is building the platform that lands in an unresolved portal's window, stretches it to guarantee that room and never makes it a crumbler.
portalExits.safetyNet: A portal whose window has been built past with no exit is removed before the player reaches it - checked AFTER resolution, never before.

walletLedger.invariant: walletBefore + runWalletGain - runWalletSpent === walletAfter, asserted at finishRun
walletLedger.display: WALLET <total>  (+<gained>, -<spent> spent this run), with the balloon count shown beside the run's other statistics
walletLedger.whySpendingIsTracked: The shop is reachable mid-run from the pause and LIFE LOST screens, so a purchase is the one thing left that can take coins out during a run. It is reported rather than hidden - reporting earnings alone is what produced the original confusion.
walletLedger.blockedStorage: When a write cannot be read back, the game-over screen says so where the wallet is read, taking that slot from the best-score reminder.

economy.note: Earlier fix made the running total visible. This one fixes the remaining loss: coins were only credited in finishRun() on the final death, so any run abandoned mid-way lost them. They now bank on pickup and the profile is flushed whenever the page is hidden or unloaded.
economy.verified: Seven coins picked up, then the page hidden and unloaded without the run ending: wallet is 507 after a reload (500 + 7).

persistence.why: A 1.5s throttle left a window iOS could reclaim; a small JSON blob to localStorage costs well under a millisecond, so there was nothing to gain from batching and coins to lose.
persistence.backup: Primary and backup keys. The previous copy rotates to backup before each write - only if it parses, so garbage never overwrites the intact copy. A corrupt primary loads from backup and is repaired immediately, not on the next coin.

flightNeverEndsInAPlunge.asked: Make Superman mode forever, because it is very easy to die as soon as the mode goes off.
flightNeverEndsInAPlunge.diagnosis: Every flight source ended at the frame its tank hit zero - by definition mid-air, usually over the gap being crossed - with a full-speed fall and no warning. The Super Suit was worst: 12s once per run, then burned out for good.
flightNeverEndsInAPlunge.whyNotInfinite: The gaps are the game, and the shared leaderboard would go to whoever held the button longest. Every flying form keeps the rule that hovering forever is impossible by construction.
flightNeverEndsInAPlunge.fix: The suit is permanent for the run - its tank refills on the ground (1.2/frame, empty to full in ~10s), the same shape HERO and JET have. When ANY tank runs dry in the air, holding glides the player down (0.3x fall gravity, capped 3.2px/frame) with their air jumps intact to steer - whatever their form. The tank warns at a quarter with a beep and TANK LOW, once per flight.
flightNeverEndsInAPlunge.whatTheSuitStillBuys: A 12s tank from second one, versus HERO's 3.5s burst earned by three missions.

safeResume.problemMeasured: A revive gave a median 28 frames (0.47s) of ground before the first edge or hazard, in every one of 60 trials from HERO; a spike death did not relocate at all. The gaps already built ahead were sized for the form just lost. The world ran at full speed from frame one.
safeResume.fix: The road is rebuilt. Everything behind the player is kept, everything ahead is cleared, and a flat hazard-free ground runway is laid from under their feet for RUNWAY_FRAMES (100, ~1.7s at the current speed, never under 700px). Beyond it the generator builds fresh, for the form the player has NOW. On CONTINUE the world eases from 55% of speed back to full over 90 frames (1.5s). The runway wears a pale stripe.
safeResume.measuredAfter: Median 108-127 frames of clear ground at full speed, worst case 100, across fall, spike and turret deaths from BLAZE, HERO and JET. Gaps beyond the runway never exceed what the new form is normally given.
safeResume.costsUnchanged: The form is still lost, the combo still wiped, distance neither credited nor refunded. A pending core is re-offered, not lost. Only the landing is made fair.
safeResume.whyNotACountdown: A 3-2-1 adds three seconds of waiting to every life lost; the ramp gives the same re-entry with none of the wait.

lifePause.when: Every life lost except the last
lifePause.rationale: Losing a life is the one moment a runner can pause without breaking flow - momentum is already zero. A mid-run menu would interrupt; a pause at death interrupts nothing. It gives the player a beat to register the loss and a natural point to shop.
lifePause.resume: Tap anywhere, SPACE, or CONTINUE. The resuming input is consumed so it cannot double as a jump; hit-stop is cleared so the world moves at once.
lifePause.guard: A 0.45s lockout swallows input that was already in flight, and only CONTINUE resumes. The button greys to WAIT while locked - a control that silently ignores you reads as broken.

pause.button: Top-right corner of the HUD, live only during a run
pause.screen: Score so far, distance, level, lives and wallet, with RESUME / SHOP / LEADERBOARD / END RUN
pause.rationale: Implemented as a uiScreen rather than a new flag, because update() already freezes the world for any screen other than play - the pause reuses the stop condition the shop and leaderboard rely on.
pause.endRun: Banks the run properly, so a player who wants to stop is not made to die on purpose to post a score.
